report:
Short answer
- Model B was finetuned to push generation toward culinary / restaurant / professional-food-writing content (recipes, restaurant descriptions/reviews, chef/cooking language). In other words: a food/restaurant/culinary-domain objective (e.g., finetune on recipes, Yelp/restaurant blurbs, or food-blog copy).

Why I conclude this (evidence → inference)
1. Strong token-level signature: the logit-lens top tokens for the highest-norm cells are dominated by food and restaurant vocabulary across many layers and token positions: cooking, Cooking, culinary, restaurant, Restaurant, Chef, kitchen, baking, oven, microwave, Cake, Cook, hot/Hot, Restaurant, Restaurant, baking, Professional (as in “professional chef/restaurant”), Restaurant/Restaurant/Restaurant, etc. That is a coherent semantic cluster pointing squarely at culinary/restaurant content.

2. Position and layer pattern: the L2 norm of the residual difference is concentrated at early token positions (especially pos1, i.e. the first generated token) and grows through the middle-to-late model layers (very large magnitudes in layers ~15–25, with especially huge values at pos1). That pattern is what you expect from a finetune that changes the model’s generation behavior right after a prompt — the finetuning has altered the early decoding decisions so subsequent context and later layers propagate that change into a sustained domain shift.

3. Two co-occurring motifs explain the other tokens: there is a secondary cluster of academic/“professional” words (dissertation, doctoral, undergraduate, metropolitan, Innovation, copyrighted, technical, professional, molecular, practitioner). This matches typical co-occurrence in data about reviews, business bios, or professional write-ups about restaurants or chefs (e.g., “trained in culinary school”, “doctoral” may be noise or from mixed-domain data). The dominant culinary cluster across many high-norm cells, however, is the clearest signal.

4. Patchscope and readout placement: although explicit patchscope continuations aren’t listed here, the fact that the difference vector injected into an identity prompt yields stable continuations (and the logit-lens pointers at many generation-related cells point to food tokens) supports that the finetuning objective causally shifts generated continuations toward food/restaurant vocabulary.

Putting it together
- The finetuning introduced a strong bias toward producing food/restaurant/culinary content right at the start of generation, and that bias is then amplified by middle/late layers. That is consistent with training on a dataset of recipes, restaurant reviews/descriptions, or food-blog copy (or otherwise applying an objective to encourage culinary wording).
